skill.name: email-quality-auditor
skill.description: Audits one email program before release using the 20-item SEND framework, evidence checks, veto controls, and deterministic scoring when available.
skill.summary: Assess email safety, evidence quality, and release readiness with the SEND framework.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: All 33 static alerts were adjudicated as false positives. The evidence consists of Markdown syntax, fixed repository references, metadata URLs, and a fixed local Git lookup without user-controlled arguments. No semantic threat or prompt injection was found.

content.value_statement: Email teams can miss authentication, consent, suppression, claim, and measurement failures before release. This skill applies an evidence-based SEND audit and reports a score, gate verdict, or exact evidence gaps.
actual_capabilities: Audits one promotional, retention, cold-outbound, or newsletter program across a normalized observation window.
Evaluates 20 SEND criteria covering sender integrity, engagement, nurture, and direct outcomes.
Checks authentication, consent provenance, suppression handling, claims, and disclosures for release-blocking failures.
Separates observed failures from unknown evidence and conditionally inapplicable criteria.
Reports context, evidence confidence, detailed findings, score state, verdict, gaps, and fix owners.
Uses the deterministic scorer when available and returns an unscored result when required runtime components are missing.
limitations: Does not send email or modify provider settings, consent records, claims, or suppression data.
Cannot produce a comparable score when required evidence or the root scoring runtime is unavailable.
Does not prove inbox placement from DNS records alone.
Open and CTOR metrics remain proxy evidence and require MPP segmentation.

use_cases.title: Gate a campaign release
use_cases.description: Review a planned broadcast for authentication, consent, suppression, claims, and outcome evidence before approval.

use_cases.title: Verify compliance controls
use_cases.description: Trace lawful basis, opt-out behavior, and live suppression handling against dated evidence.

use_cases.title: Establish a quality baseline
use_cases.description: Score a newsletter or lifecycle program across SEND dimensions and identify accountable fix owners.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic preflight audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this newsletter before release. Review the supplied message, audience source, unsubscribe flow, and authentication evidence. List blockers, unknowns, and required next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with limited campaign evidence

prompt_templates.title: Review sender and consent controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this promotional send for SPF, DKIM, DMARC, consent provenance, and live suppression handling. Cite each evidence source and observation date.

prompt_templates.title: Score a complete SEND profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this retention program using the last 90 days. Declare provider, market, list age, MPP share, and outcome truth set. Score every applicable SEND criterion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Full program baseline with complete exports

prompt_templates.title: Trace a release veto
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this cold-outbound program and trace every possible SEND veto to DNS, consent events, suppression state, or approved claims. Separate failures from unknowns and assign fix owners.

output_examples.input: Audit a newsletter with complete evidence, a score of 81, and no veto failures.
output_examples.output: Verdict: SHIP. The audit is complete with a final score of 81. No blocking control failed, and all required evidence is present.

output_examples.input: Audit a promotional program with broken authentication and a raw score of 76.
output_examples.output: Verdict: FIX. Authentication failed the SEND-S1 veto, so the final score is capped at 59. The sender owner must correct alignment before release.

output_examples.input: Audit a send when consent provenance is missing.
output_examples.output: Verdict: UNDECIDED. Consent provenance remains unknown, so the audit needs input and no comparable score is issued.

best_practices: Provide dated DNS, provider, consent, suppression, content, and outcome evidence for the same observation window.
Declare the program profile, provider, market, list age, MPP share, and observation date before scoring.
Treat missing evidence as unknown and provide reasons for every conditionally inapplicable criterion.
anti_patterns: Do not treat missing evidence as a passing or partially passing control.
Do not infer inbox placement from SPF, DKIM, or DMARC records alone.
Do not request a full release verdict from a send-only review with incomplete program evidence.

faq.question: Which email programs can this skill audit?
faq.answer: It supports promotional, retention, cold-outbound, and newsletter profiles.

faq.question: Does the skill send emails?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and never executes a send.

faq.question: Can it change provider or consent settings?
faq.answer: No. It does not modify provider settings, consent records, suppression data, or claims.

faq.question: What evidence should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide dated authentication, consent, suppression, provider, engagement, content, and outcome records for one normalized window.

faq.question: What happens when evidence is missing?
faq.answer: Applicable items become unknown. The skill returns an undecided or needs-input result instead of inventing a score.

faq.question: Can it run without the repository scorer?
faq.answer: It can collect typed observations, but it must return an unscored result without the required deterministic runtime.
